page.layout: Running head at top: page number at left, title centred. One column of running text below. Under the text, four ruled blank lines (no printing). No marginal notes.

main_text.p: depressio,& subjugatio concupiscentiæ,quâ producatur teneritas cordis, & animæ puritas. 5 Peregri-natio, quæ exitus è Mundo & itionis in occursum futuri typus est, nec alio plerique eorum qui in ea observantur ritus,tendunt,quàm probationi & tentationi hominis,an ea quæ ipsi mandata sint sectari velit; quales sunt Cursus & Properatio in circuitione [(aabæ] & jactus lapillorum. Quod verò ad observationem diei Veneris & Festorum, instituta sunt ea ad Congregationem populi, quo conveni-ant, & se mutuò visant, & in iis à laborum tædiis quiescant. Circumcisio autem injunctio est; cui inest tentatio & probatio, & deditio sui [Deo] Quod ad prohibitionem Morticinii, & sanguinis, in eo quod horreat ea animus,& refugiat natura, satis est quod abstinentiam ab illis ut necessariam suadeat.

page.notes: Text begins mid-sentence ("depressio"), so the first paragraph is a continuation. Printed as "depressio" and "fubjugatio" with long s, rendered as plain s. The "5" before "Peregrinatio" is an inline section number in the text, not a heading. A small ink spot sits after "Peregri-" and another after "animus,", both stains, not printed marks. Spacing after "tendunt," and "animus," is irregular in print. The page has no catchword or signature.
